question: On the boards where Q04.2 finds that router.autorouter.pass_controller=quantum-stop stops before the default run's last score improvement, does quantum-stop with its registered defaults (grace 0, checks 2, quantum max(1.0, 0.01 * |best score|)) cut the routing wall time by at least 20 % without raising unrouted, vias or clearance violations on any board, and with the unrouted total within the set's noise?
rule_text: N02 (docs/roadmap/tasks/N02-keep-rule-for-defaults.md), the speed clause: the candidate passes when (1) the hard guards hold on every board: via_in_pad = 0 in the candidate, and unrouted, vias and clearance_violations of the candidate not above the baseline's (a rise of 1 on one board fails, whatever the noise; the checklist's 'no regression in unrouted on any board'); (2) the unrouted total over the distinct boards is within the set's noise (sqrt of the sum of the per-board bands squared) and no board is worse by more than twice its band; (3) the summed wall_seconds drops by at least 20 %. Determinism (D2): routing is deterministic at the pin, so one run per arm; the candidate's run on each board is repeated once and its SES must be byte-identical (tools/determinism-check.sh on canary-pwr-pours1, Q04.2). The checklist's drc_real guard is clearance_violations here: the boards are DSN files without KiCad boards, so Freerouting's own DRC grades them. pass_rule below is the parser's paired rule, kept only so the file validates; it does not decide.

noise.formula: max(2, ceil(0.05 * connections)) for every other board (N02's rule until Q12.4 measures it)
noise.source: N02: the canary-pwr variants' spread of +-10

defaults.changed: only through an amendment of this file, with the reason; tests/quality_stop_rule.rs pins them

default.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 2; one build for both arms, its --version git sha in Q04.4's note), the default profile
default.what: baseline: Java's pass controller, the passes unlimited

quantum-stop.what: candidate: Q04.1's stop rule around Java's controller, plus Q04.5's repeat stop (amendment 1)

boards.set: tools/bench/sets/quick-benchmark.txt (amendment 2; registered: tools/bench/sets/benchmark.txt and the in-repository rows of tools/bench/sets/owner.txt)
boards.procedure: Q04.2 routes every board below with both arms (target/orchestrator/q04/q04-heavy.sh: the commands above, one run at a time, quiet machine) and records the pass of the default run's last score improvement. Q04.4's rows are exactly the boards where quantum-stop stopped before that pass; the others are not rows (their sessions are equal, which Q04.2 checks). Before any Q04.4 number is judged, one amendment narrows 'files' to those rows, quoting Q04.2's table; nothing else may change in it. The canary-pwr variants count as one board (gate collect --group fixtures/canary-pwr/=canary-pwr). If fewer than 3 distinct boards remain, the gate cannot pass (min_boards 3): the numbers are reported in Q04.4 and quantum-stop stays an opt-in setting with no DIVERGENCES 'kept' line.

grading: freerouting-dev ses-diff statistics of each SES imported into its DSN (gate collect: unrouted = connections.incomplete_count, vias = vias.total_count, clearance_violations = clearance_violations.total_count) and gate collect's via_in_pad; wall_seconds is the CLI run's wall time as target/orchestrator/q04/q04-heavy.sh prints it (amendment 2: no quiet-machine condition; Q04.2's run of each arm on a row is that row's registered run)
keep_rule: if the candidate passes, docs/DIVERGENCES.md gets a line with the time saved on canary-pwr and the setting stays opt-in (unset in both profiles) until N05 decides enhanced; if it fails, Q04.4's note keeps the numbers and the cause, and quantum-stop stays an opt-in pass controller only if N02's keep-or-delete rule allows it
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per board, plus the candidate's determinism rerun on canary-pwr-pours1; tuning the defaults needs an amendment before a new run, never after a number of that run

amendments.what: arm quantum-stop also sets router.quantum_stop.repeat=true (Q04.5): its command gains --router.quantum_stop.repeat=true and its settings list the option; the candidate is therefore Q04.1's restore-check rule plus the repeat stop, and Q04.2's table of rows (the boards where the candidate stopped before the default run's last score improvement) is read with that command. Nothing else changes: the defaults, the guards, the rule, the pool of boards and the speed clause stay as registered
amendments.why: Q04.2's short check found boards whose passes leave one and the same board (Issue093-interf_u: 18 passes, one board; CNH_Functional_Tester_1: 4 distinct boards), where the history never holds 8 boards, Java runs no restore check and quantum-stop alone saves nothing. The repeat stop (a pass that leaves the board with the state hash it started with ends the loop, StopReason::Repeat, logged 'Stopping the auto-router (quantum-stop repeat).') is the cheapest rule for them: on Issue093-interf_u it stops at pass 2 of 18 with a byte-identical session (tests/quality_stop_rule.rs, issue093_interf_u_stops_at_the_first_repeat_with_an_identical_session). The amendment is written before any Q04.4 number exists: no row of the Q04.4 table has been measured. Which of the two rules ended a run is read from its log line, so the numbers can still be attributed

amendments.after: the registration and amendment 1; before any Q04.2 or Q04.4 run under the amended candidate (Q04.2's short check of 2026-10-18 ran the candidate without the repeat stop, and Q04.5's spot checks are not runs of this registration)
amendments.reason: decided 2026-10-20: measurement runs stay a few minutes: every row routes in well under a minute except one canary-pwr row, the whole run takes minutes, no quiet-machine wall-time condition. The registered pool (16 benchmark boards and 5 canary-pwr variants, two to three arms each plus Q04.4's own runs and the determinism rerun) would take hours
amendments.changes: (1) Rows: boards.files keeps the 8 benchmark boards whose longest recorded route took at most 25 s and canary-pwr-pours1 (tools/bench/sets/quick-benchmark.txt, which gives each time and the target/orchestrator/<dir>/ it came from: 0.1 to 23.3 s, canary-pwr-pours1 97.6 to 104.2 s in P04's bench runs); dropped for their route time: bm01 49.3 s, CPU-85 61.7 s, z10_module 200.9 s, smoothieboard 226.2 s, LogicBoard_smt 434.7 s, GP8B 500.4 s, coldfire 550.4 s, contribution-board 702.4 s, canary-pwr-pours2, -pours3, -pours-as-planes and -2026-10-15-1747-unpoured (107.8 to 357.4 s). The procedure is unchanged otherwise: Q04.2 routes every row with both arms, and Q04.4's rows are those where quantum-stop stopped before the default run's last score improvement, narrowed by an amendment before any Q04.4 verdict; min_boards 3 is unchanged. (2) Runs: Q04.2's run of each arm on a row (target/orchestrator/q04/q04-heavy.sh, the registered commands, one run at a time) is that row's registered Q04.4 run, so Q04.4 routes nothing again; its wall_seconds is the script's printed wall time, without the quiet-machine condition; the speed clause (summed wall_seconds down at least 20 %) is unchanged. (3) Determinism: the candidate's rerun stays on canary-pwr-pours1 (tools/determinism-check.sh). (4) Every route runs under ulimit -v 8000000, with timeout 600 for canary-pwr-pours1 and timeout 120 for the other rows; a timeout leaves the measurement incomplete. (5) Engine: one release build of main at the run. Nothing else changes: question, defaults, metrics, totals block, guards
